questions.question_text: What is the multiplicative inverse of the rational number 3/4?
Explain why every integer is a rational number with an example.
questions.sample_answer: Every integer is a rational number because it can be expressed in the form p/q where p is the integer and q is 1. For example, the integer 5 can be written as 5/1, which is a rational number.
expected_points: Integer as a special case of rational number
Example of an integer as a rational number

questions.question_text: If a and b are two rational numbers, then what can be said about the result of a + b, a - b and a * b?
questions.sample_answer: The result of a + b, a - b and a * b will always be a rational number because rational numbers are closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication.
expected_points: Rational numbers are closed under addition
Rational numbers are closed under subtraction
Rational numbers are closed under multiplication

questions.question_text: Represent the rational numbers 3/5, -2/3 and 7/10 on a number line and arrange them in ascending order.
questions.sample_answer: To represent these rational numbers on a number line, first we find the equivalent rational numbers with a common denominator, which is the LCM of 5, 3 and 10, i.e., 30. So, 3/5 = 18/30, -2/3 = -20/30 and 7/10 = 21/30. Now, we can represent these numbers on the number line. The ascending order of these numbers is -2/3, 7/10, 3/5.
expected_points: Converting rational numbers to equivalent form with common denominator
Representing the numbers on the number line
Arranging the numbers in ascending order
